title: Racing Joe Louis from Flint to Detroit
summary: Joe Louis followed the band in his car, hit 110 miles per hour and a policeman stopped him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: We were doing one nighters and we were going to play Flint, Michigan, you know? So he followed us in his Lincoln. Joe Louis. When we got through the dance, Joe Louis asked me and Duke and Sonny Greer -- we're going to a little cabaret, you know? And he got mad because he was charging, he was charging because Joe Louis was going to be there and he didn't like that. He said you are going to try to make money out of me, and so forth -- so he just didn't go in.

So we started back to Detroit, and he was trying to follow one of those -- I know the car, it was a real fast car, and he was doing 110 miles an hour. Oh my Lord, and that Sonny Greer was full of whiskey and would say, "Take them Champ! Take them!"
And a policeman stopped him and when he found out it was Joe Louis, but he still told us not to go that fast in there because you'll never live to be a champion, you know?
Uh huh. He didn't give him a ticket?
And every time I used to see after that -- No, no ticket -- Joe Louis, I used to tell him, "How about that 110 miles?" He used to laugh and say that when he
got to his hotel he had little things in his drawer, you know? I was scared to death.
